batchName: Middle Republic: The Gracchi (133-121 BCE) - Easy Batch 2

questions.question: What emergency measure did the Senate pass for the first time in 121 BC?
options: A list of outlaws who could be killed
A formal declaration of war on Gaius
A 'final decree' to defend the state by any means
questions.explanation: The senatus consultum ultimum urged the consul Opimius to defend the state by any means necessary.
questions.sourceQuote: It passed its first "final decree" (*senatus consultum ultimum*), urging him to defend the state by any means necessary.

questions.question: Which relative of Tiberius helped run the land commission after his death?
questions.explanation: Tiberius's land law survived his murder, and the commission kept working, staffed by his allies, including Gaius.
questions.sourceQuote: The commission it created kept working, staffed by his allies, including his younger brother Gaius Gracchus.

questions.question: What happened to the bodies of Tiberius and his supporters after they were killed?
options: They were thrown into the Tiber
They were returned to their families
They were displayed in the Forum
They were buried on the Capitoline
questions.explanation: The bodies were dumped in the river that runs through Rome. The men had been beaten to death with stones, wooden chairs and other blunt objects.
questions.sourceQuote: They were beaten to death with stones, wooden chairs and other blunt objects, and their bodies were thrown into the Tiber, the river that runs through Rome.

questions.question: Which year do ancient and modern writers see as the start of the Roman Republic's decline?
questions.explanation: 133 BC was the year of Tiberius Gracchus's murder. A famous Roman orator later wrote that Tiberius had divided one people into two factions.
questions.sourceQuote: Both ancient and modern writers see 133 BC, the year of Tiberius Gracchus's murder, as the start of the Republic's decline.

questions.question: How did Gaius Gracchus change the way speeches were given in the Forum?
options: He delivered his speeches in Greek
He had heralds read his written speeches
He spoke standing in a war chariot
He faced the crowd instead of the senate house
questions.explanation: By turning towards the crowd, Gaius in effect turned his back on the Senate. He ranked among the greatest Roman orators of his age.
questions.sourceQuote: He even changed how speeches were given in the Forum: instead of facing the senate house, he turned towards the crowd, in effect turning his back on the Senate.

questions.question: What surviving objects let historians trace the work of the Gracchan land commission?
options: Boundary stones carved with commissioners' names
Bronze coins stamped with land grants
questions.explanation: Boundary stones called cippi, carved with the commissioners' names, have been found all over southern Italy.
questions.sourceQuote: Its progress can still be traced through boundary stones (*cippi*) carved with the commissioners' names, found all over southern Italy.

questions.question: In 122 BC, Gaius Gracchus proposed granting Roman citizenship to which group?
questions.explanation: It was his boldest proposal, and it also offered new rights to other Italians. A rival tribune vetoed it.
questions.sourceQuote: In 122 BC Gaius Gracchus, serving a second year as tribune, made his boldest proposal: citizenship for the Latins, Rome's closest allies, and new rights for other Italians.

questions.question: Which body did Tiberius Gracchus bypass when he took his land bill straight to the Plebeian Council?
questions.explanation: Custom expected a bill to be discussed in the Senate first, but Tiberius went directly to the assembly of ordinary citizens.
questions.sourceQuote: He took his bill straight to the Plebeian Council (*concilium plebis*), the assembly of ordinary citizens, without first consulting the Senate (*senatus*), as custom expected.

questions.question: Which king's bequest of his kingdom and treasury to Rome did Tiberius want to use for his land scheme?
questions.explanation: The king of Pergamum left his kingdom and treasury to Rome, and Tiberius proposed tapping this windfall after the Senate starved the land commission of money.
questions.sourceQuote: Then news arrived that the king of Pergamum, a rich Greek kingdom in western Asia Minor, had died and left his treasury and kingdom to Rome.

questions.question: What high office did the father of the Gracchi brothers hold twice?
questions.explanation: Their father was twice consul, one of the two heads of state elected each year. He also served as censor and celebrated two triumphs.
questions.sourceQuote: Their father, also called Tiberius, had twice been consul, one of the two heads of state elected each year.
